description.narrative:
Impact goal Providing concrete solutions to transform and improve the living conditions and opportunities of the population and territories affected by the armed conflict, thereby contributing to peace.
Outcomes: 1.Learn and innovate: which implies a raising awareness and knowledge strategy that includes collecting, systematizing and producing knowledge about business models and actions that contribute to peace and offer useful inputs to public and business decision-making. 2.Inclusive business: which aims to include, as competitive suppliers, the productive organizations of vulnerable populations, located in conflict affected regions, in the value chain of anchor companies. 3.Inspire: which aims to promote and visibilize the role of the business sector in peace building in Colombia. The three pillars include activities at national and regional levels.

Detta är ett gemensamt program utvecklat av Andi Foundation, Ideas for Peace Foundation och Emprender Paz Corporation för att främja större engagemang från den privata sektorn i att tillhandahålla konkreta lösningar för att förändra och förbättra levnadsvillkoren för befolkningen och för de territorier som påverkats av den väpnade konflikten, och därmed bidra till fred.
Förslaget syftar till att samordna de tre institutionernas ansträngningar för att främja ett integrerat tillvägagångssätt som inkluderar input och information till beslutsfattare och allmänheten, bygger broar mellan nationella och regionala regeringar och företag, ökar medvetenheten bland privata företag om goda exempel på ansvarsfullt företagande och den påverkan de kan ha i fredsbyggandet, och slutligen, som främjar kommersiella förbindelser mellan stora företag och mindre bönder från konfliktdrabbade regioner och därav stimulerar ekonomiska möjligheter i dessa regioner. Detta är en fortsättningsfas på Sida’s insatser med ID-nummer: 55190013; 52060045; 55190020 och 10924

This is a project support developed by Andi Foundation, Ideas for Peace Foundation and Emprender Paz Corporation to promote greater involvement by the private sector in providing concrete solutions to transform and improve the living conditions of the population and territories affected by the armed conflict, thereby contributing to peace.
The contribution aims to coordinate efforts of the three organisations to promote an integral approach that includes inputs and information for policy makers as well as the public opinion, builds bridges between the national and regional governments and enterprises, raises awareness among private companies of good examples of responsible business conduct together with the impact they could play in peace building, and, finally, promotes commercial links between large companies and small peasant farmers from conflict affected regions thus stimulating economic opportunities in selected regions.
This is a continuation phase of Sida’s contributions with ID-numbers: 55190013, 52060045, 55190020 and 10924.

description.narrative:
The Embassy's overall assessment is that the three partners have achieved the intended goals and that the report and its annexes have adequately and completely summarized the activities, results, lessons learned, and risks.
Regarding the first component of Learn and innovate: the FIP has made significant progress in all the planned outputs reaching 50% of expected goals. This confirms they insistence in the need of funding as the goals for three years could be reached in two. This component aims at raising awareness and knowledge building strategy that includes collecting, systematizing and producing knowledge on business models and actions that contribute to peace and provide useful inputs for public and business decision-making.
Regarding the second component of Inclusive business: In this component ANDI Foundation aims to include, the productive organizations of vulnerable populations, located in conflict affected regions, as competitive suppliers in the value chain of anchor companies. They already have 19 of the 30 targeted anchor companies working in pre-feasibility, feasibility and implementation phases. Regarding the productive organizations they have already identified 162. Regarding the allies, they have already included 43 which reported own private investment of 271 million COP (Approximately 64,000USD). ANDI also presents significant progress in gender indicators as they have already included 177 of the targeted 200 women as part of the productive units. As regards the environment, they have already 4 of the 15 productive units with climate change mitigation measures and 74 participants have received technical assistance to promote these mitigation measures and action plans.
Regarding the third component of Inspire, the Emprender Paz award held the 17th award ceremony on November 27, 2024, selecting 4 additional winers (Ekofil, Caryo, Marimbea, Red de Frio) among 127 nominees and 11 finalists. These initiatives had a positive impact in 30 of the country's 32 departments, directly benefiting more than 575,000 people. The initiatives submitted came from organizations across a wide range of sectors (43% services, 20% agribusiness, 13% agriculture, 6% industry, 17% commerce, and 3% manufacturing) and sizes (69% micro, 10% small, 4% medium, 17% large). The 11 finalists have invested US$2.3 million in the winning initiatives, demonstrating their commitment and ownership. In addition to media recognition, the four winners have received technical assistance over the past year to improve their initiatives. Only one of these initiatives has been satisfactorily completed in 2024, and the other three will be developed in 2025.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
